title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 393 (Company's failure to comply with provisions of this Chapter not to affect validity of contracts, etc.)

content.overview: Failure by a company to comply with Chapter XXII does not affect the validity of any contract, dealing or transaction entered into by the company or its liability to be sued thereon. However, the company is not entitled to bring a suit, claim a set-off, make a counter-claim or institute a legal proceeding in respect of such contract, dealing or transaction until it has complied with the applicable provisions of the Act.
content.glance: Non-compliance does not invalidate contracts; company cannot enforce them until it complies.
content.study: Section 393 protects third parties and the company's liability to be sued, while imposing a procedural disability on the defaulting company until compliance is achieved.

sections.heading: Validity preserved
sections.body: Contracts remain valid despite Chapter XXII non-compliance.

sections.heading: Procedural disability
sections.body: Company cannot sue, set-off, counter-claim or proceed until it complies.
